title: Travellers described a flourishing Vijayanagara capital at Hampi
body: From the 14th to the 16th century, travellers wrote about the temples and palaces of Vijayanagara at what is now Hampi in Karnataka. The city was sacked in 1565 and ceased to be the imperial capital.
takeaway: Descriptions made while the city was inhabited help explain ruins whose streets and monuments survive today.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Group of Monuments at Hampi (1986)
visual: stone temple columns and ruined streets across Hampi's boulder-strewn landscape

title: Mahabalipuram's Pallava artists carved a story into open rock
body: On Tamil Nadu's Coromandel coast, Pallava kings founded sanctuaries carved in the seventh and eighth centuries CE. The monumental Descent of the Ganges relief is exposed outdoors on the rock face.
takeaway: An image on a cliff can be experienced as part of a public landscape, at a scale a portable object cannot match.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (1984)
visual: a broad rock face carved with an elephant and small figures on the Coromandel coast
